title: minitrap
text: minitrap provides two purrr-style function adverbs, mtrap_safely() and mtrap_quietly(), that trap errors or console output instead of letting them reach the console. See the README for the full API reference and scope notes; this page walks through both in action.

title: minitrap
text:
mtrap_safely()
Wrap a function so a call that would normally error instead returns a list with the error captured alongside a NULL result:

safe_log <- mtrap_safely(log)
safe_log(-1)

Warning in .f(...): NaNs produced


$result
[1] NaN

$error
NULL


A successful call returns the result with error set to NULL:

safe_log(10)

$result
[1] 2.302585

$error
NULL

title: minitrap
text:
mtrap_quietly()
Wrap a function so printed output, warnings, and messages are captured instead of shown:

quiet_fn <- mtrap_quietly(function() {
  message("starting")
  warning("using a default")
  42
})
quiet_fn()

$result
[1] 42

$output
[1] ""

$warnings
[1] "using a default"

$messages
[1] "starting\n"


mtrap_quietly() does not catch errors – compose with mtrap_safely() for that:

robust_fn <- mtrap_safely(mtrap_quietly(function() stop("boom")))
robust_fn()

$result
NULL

$error
<simpleError in .f(...): boom>

title: minicli
text:
minicli is a minimal stand-in for the small slice of cli most packages actually use: coloured alert messages, unicode symbols with an ascii fallback, a rule, and a bullet list. See the README for the full API reference and capability-detection details; this page walks through each piece.
One thing to note about the output below: Quarto/knitr renders are detected as a non-terminal (getOption("knitr.in.progress")), so ANSI colour is automatically disabled here – the alerts below print in plain text with their symbol prefix, exactly as they would in a captured log or a non-interactive session, rather than showing colour codes as literal text.

title: minicli
text:
Alerts
mcli_alert_success()/_danger()/_warning()/_info() are thin message() wrappers with a symbol prefix; extra ... arguments are passed through sprintf():

mcli_alert_success("Wrote %d files to %s", 3, "output/")

✔ Wrote 3 files to output/



mcli_alert_warning("Skipped %d rows with missing values", 12)

⚠ Skipped 12 rows with missing values



mcli_alert_danger("Failed to connect to %s", "database")

✖ Failed to connect to database



mcli_alert_info("Using default configuration")

ℹ Using default configuration

title: minicli
text:
Symbols
mcli_symbol() looks up a named symbol, respecting unicode availability:

mcli_symbol("tick")

[1] "✔"

mcli_symbol("cross")

[1] "✖"

mcli_symbol("arrow_right")

[1] "→"

title: minicli
text:
Rule
mcli_rule() prints a horizontal divider, optionally with a centred title:

mcli_rule("Summary")

─────────────────────────────────── Summary ────────────────────────────────────

title: minicli
text:
Bullets
mcli_bullets() prints a simple bulleted list, one entry per line:

mcli_bullets(c("one", "two", "three"))

• one
• two
• three

title: minicli
text:
Colours and styles
mcli_col_*()/mcli_style_*() wrap text in an ANSI code, and are no-ops (returning the text unchanged) whenever ANSI is disabled – which, per the note above, is always true on this page:

identical(mcli_col_red("danger"), "danger")

[1] TRUE

identical(mcli_style_bold("emphasis"), "emphasis")

[1] TRUE

title: minis
text:
A collection of small, standalone, zero-runtime-dependency R components (“minis”), each shipped as a single .R file with its own drop-in test suite. When a package needs a little bit of cli-style formatting, or a little bit of purrr-style mapping, or some other small convenience, but taking on the full dependency isn’t worth it, grab the relevant mini and copy it straight into R/.
See the repository README for the full philosophy and usage instructions. This site collects worked-example vignettes for minis that have one; minis without a vignette yet are still listed below, linking straight to their GitHub README.

title: minis
text:

title: minimap
text: minimap provides purrr-style mapping functions – mmap_map(), mmap_map2(), mmap_imap(), mmap_walk(), mmap_iwalk(), and the type-stable mmap_map_dbl()/mmap_map_lgl()/mmap_map_chr() – built entirely on lapply()/vapply(). See the README for the full API reference and scope notes; this page walks through each in action.

title: minimap
text:
mmap_map()
Applies a function to each element of a list or vector, always returning a list, with names preserved:

mmap_map(1:3, function(x) x + 1)

[[1]]
[1] 2

[[2]]
[1] 3

[[3]]
[1] 4



mmap_map(c(a = 1, b = 2), function(x) x * 10)

$a
[1] 10

$b
[1] 20

title: minimap
text:
Type-stable variants
mmap_map_dbl(), mmap_map_lgl(), and mmap_map_chr() return an atomic vector instead of a list, erroring if .f doesn’t return a length-1 value of the expected type for every element:

mmap_map_dbl(1:3, function(x) x + 1)

[1] 2 3 4



mmap_map_lgl(1:5, function(x) x %% 2 == 0)

[1] FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE



mmap_map_dbl(1:3, function(x) c(x, x))

Error in `vapply()`:
! values must be length 1,
 but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 2

title: minimap
text:
mmap_map2() and mmap_imap()
mmap_map2() walks two same-length vectors in parallel:

mmap_map2(1:3, 4:6, function(x, y) x + y)

[[1]]
[1] 5

[[2]]
[1] 7

[[3]]
[1] 9


mmap_imap() walks a named vector together with its names, passing .f the element then its name:

mmap_imap(c(a = 1, b = 2), function(val, name) paste0(name, "=", val))

$a
[1] "a=1"

$b
[1] "b=2"

title: minimap
text:
mmap_walk() and mmap_iwalk()
Both run .f for its side effects only, returning .x invisibly:

mmap_walk(1:3, function(x) cat("value:", x, "\n"))

value: 1 
value: 2 
value: 3 



mmap_iwalk(c(a = 1, b = 2), function(val, name) cat(name, "->", val, "\n"))

a -> 1 
b -> 2
